title: Hour Commit Decoupling
subtitle: Splitting player-facing progression from durable hour commit
summary: Today one state machine owns both the player-visible hour and its durable commit, so a half-failed commit leaves the two out of sync. We split it into a Frontend FSM that owns progression and a Backend FSM that owns the commit lifecycle, with an explicit FAILED state and a retry path.
background: The simulation advances one in-world hour at a time. A single frontend state machine owns both player-facing progression and the durable commit of an hour's results. When a commit fails halfway the frontend has already advanced, the two views of the world diverge, and operators recover by hand-editing session_cache.
goals: Separate command orchestration from durable state commit
Make retry and partial-failure handling explicit and observable
Let scenario plugins hook the commit lifecycle without touching core code
Keep player-visible latency of a normal hour under 800ms
non_goals: Redesigning NPC memory or the prompt pipeline
Changing the public HTTP API shape in this phase

user_stories.so_that: a transient backend error is invisible to me

See the failed commit in the ops view
Re-draft and CAS write against the fresh version

user_stories.i_want: to run code before and after an hour commit
user_stories.so_that: scenario rules stay out of the engine
acceptance: A hook failure fails the commit loudly

flow.action: Call the hook inside a 200ms budget
Apply the scenario's veto or edits
Publish the outcome the hook produced

failure_paths.name: CAS write rejected
failure_paths.trigger: Concurrent write moved the session version
failure_paths.detection: CAS mismatch returned by the store, counted in commit_failed_total
failure_paths.impact: The hour is not committed; the player stays on the current hour
failure_paths.mitigation: Re-draft against the fresh version, at most twice, then park for an operator

steps.text: Transition to FAILED and publish a failure event

failure_paths.detection: Hook deadline exceeded, logged with the plugin id
failure_paths.impact: One hour fails to commit for sessions using that scenario
failure_paths.mitigation: Cancel the hook, fail the commit, disable the plugin after 3 consecutive timeouts

steps.text: Cancel the hook and mark the commit FAILED
Disable the plugin and alert the author

rollout_phases.name: Phase 1 · Scaffolding
rollout_phases.description: Introduce the Backend FSM behind a feature flag and mirror commits without acting on them.
rollout_phases.exit_criteria: Mirrored outcomes match the legacy path for 99.9% of hours over 3 days

rollout_phases.name: Phase 2 · Migration
rollout_phases.description: Move hour commit execution behind the Backend FSM, keeping the legacy path as a fallback.
rollout_phases.exit_criteria: One full release with zero fallbacks to the legacy path

rollout_phases.name: Phase 3 · Cleanup
rollout_phases.description: Delete the legacy commit path, the flag and the mirroring code.
rollout_phases.exit_criteria: No references to the legacy commit path remain

decisions.title: Two state machines instead of one
decisions.context: A single FSM owning both progression and commit cannot represent 'the player moved on but the write failed'.

alternatives.name: Single FSM owning both concerns
cons: Every commit bug is a player-visible bug

alternatives.name: Two FSMs with an explicit boundary
pros: Commit can retry without touching the player view
cons: Two things to keep in sync

alternatives.name: Event-sourced commit log with no FSM
cons: Operators lose a simple state to read

decisions.chosen: Two FSMs with an explicit boundary
decisions.reason: It makes the failure surface explicit at the smallest migration cost, and keeps a single readable state for operators.
decisions.consequences: We accept a reconciliation job and CAS versioning as the price of the boundary.

decisions.title: Plugin hooks run inline with a hard deadline
decisions.context: Scenario hooks need to observe and veto a commit, but must not be able to hang it.

alternatives.name: Async after commit
cons: Hooks cannot veto a bad commit

decisions.reason: Veto power is the whole point of the hook; 200ms fits inside the 800ms latency goal.
decisions.consequences: Slow plugins get disabled rather than allowed to degrade the engine.

risks.title: State divergence between the two FSMs
risks.impact: Player sees an hour that was never committed
risks.mitigation: CAS versioning plus a reconciliation job

risks.title: Plugin hooks slow the commit path
risks.mitigation: 200ms hook budget with a hard cancel

constraints: The public HTTP API shape cannot change this phase
Postgres is the only durable store available

open_questions.question: Should a FAILED commit auto-retry, or always wait for an operator?
Where does the retry budget live — per session or global?

glossary.definition: The durable write that advances the simulation by one in-world hour
Compare-and-set write guarded by a version token

current_state.summary: One HourFSM in engine/fsm.py owns both the player-visible hour and the durable write. Scenario hooks are compiled into the engine and session_cache is written with no version guard.
pain_points: A failed database write leaves the frontend an hour ahead of the stored state
Scenario rules cannot change without an engine release
Nothing counts failed commits, so the failure rate is unknown

changes.what: New state machine owning PREPARING → DRAFTING → COMMITTING → FAILED
changes.why: Partial failure needs a state of its own, separate from what the player sees

changes.what: Drafting, validation and persistence lifted out of the FSM
changes.why: Orchestration and execution fail for different reasons and should be separable

changes.what: Keeps player progression only; delegates the commit and waits for an ack
changes.why: It should never be the thing that decides a write succeeded

changes.what: Adds a version column and a CAS write path
changes.why: Concurrent writes are currently silent; the FSM cannot detect them

changes.what: Hooks move from compiled-in calls to a registered before/after pair with a deadline
changes.why: Scenario rules should ship without an engine release, and must not be able to hang a commit

changes.what: Publishes every commit outcome, success or failure
changes.why: Operators and the failure metric both need a feed

changes.what: Deleted once phase 2 has run one release without a fallback
changes.why: Two commit paths is exactly the ambiguity this design removes
